newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin police smash Vietnamese cigarette gang.
newsitem.headline: Berlin police smash Vietnamese cigarette gang.

text.p: Police said on Thursday they had smashed a Vietnamese cigarette smuggling ring believed to include some of the main culprits in a grisly series of murders which have brought unheard-of gangland violence to Berlin.

Almost 40 Vietnamese have been murdered in the last four years, many of them execution-style, in a territorial battle for control of a lucrative contraband cigarette racket. Half the deaths have been this year.

Berlin police said they had detained eight Vietnamese including suspected gang leader Le Duy Bao, known in the underworld as Ngoc Thien, his wife and his deputy, in their biggest ever strike against the "cigarette mafia".

Police chief Hagen Saberschinsky said the gang was believed to control two-thirds of the 1,200 peddlers selling smuggled cigarettes in Berlin -- a racket thought to cost the government a billion marks ($700 million) a year in lost tax revenues.
"This gang's structures should now no longer exist," Saberschinsky said.
Each of the street sellers was forced to pay between 1,000 and 14,000 marks a month for his territory.

The gang, which at its peak numbered 50 members, was also believed to be responsible for murdering at least nine fellow Vietnamese between March and May, including six asylum seekers tied up and shot in the head in an east Berlin apartment.

Berlin police set up a task force including Vietnamese agents to help them tackle the racketeers, who have brought gang warfare to what is normally a relatively safe city and who were smuggling in up to 10 billion cigarettes a year.
The crackdown has succeeded in making the peddlers, whose wares are mostly smuggled in from Poland, a much less common sight on streets in Berlin and other east German cities.

Most of the peddlers are members of a 40,000 strong illegal Vietnamese community -- some of them contract workers brought in by communist East Germany before 1989, many of them Vietnamese who came to take advantage of West Germany's liberal asylum laws as communist regimes collapsed across Europe in 1989-90.
The gangs take advantage of the fact that the Vietnamese have practically no chance of getting asylum here or being able to work legally.
Hanoi is gradually honouring an agreement with Bonn to accept forced repatriation of Vietnamese living here illegally.
